about: Curated Game Updates and Historical Events for Story Mode (GLOSSARY: Game Update, Historical Event, Main Circuit). DRAFT for review. Facts are restated in our own words; 'source' names the archived Liquipedia page (CC-BY-SA 3.0) or says 'verify' when the date still needs checking. Map pools only list maps that exist in the game (ADR: map pools option B): Dust, Inferno, Mirage, Nuke, Overpass, Ancient, Train, Anubis, Cache. Effects: 'weights' multiply how much an attribute counts in match strength (1.0 = unchanged) until a later update changes it again; 'form_shock' briefly disrupts every player's form (0..1); 'map_pool' adds/removes maps from the competitive pool.

entries.title: Counter-Strike 1.0 leaves beta
entries.detail: The retail release ends a year of public betas. Competitive play has already begun on the beta versions.

entries.title: Counter-Strike 1.6 arrives on Steam
entries.detail: 1.6 adds new weapons (FAMAS, Galil, shield) and moves updates to Steam. Leagues switch from 1.5 to 1.6 gradually over 2003-2004.
entries.status: confirmed (release); the competitive switch date still needs checking

entries.title: Counter-Strike: Global Offensive released
entries.detail: The Main Circuit moves from 1.6 to CS:GO over the following months. Movement, spray patterns and economy all change: expect upsets while teams adapt.

entries.title: First Valve-sponsored Major (DreamHack Winter 2013)
entries.detail: Majors become Valve-funded and the top of the calendar.

entries.title: Overpass (and Cobblestone) added
entries.detail: Cobblestone is not in the game, so only Overpass joins.
entries.status: confirmed (added to the game); verify when it entered the competitive pool

entries.title: Tec-9 accuracy buff
entries.detail: Better accuracy and less recoil make T-side pistol buys stronger.

entries.title: VAC ban wave hits professional players
entries.detail: Several pro players are banned for cheating (see the generated ban events).

entries.title: iBUYPOWER match-fixing bans
entries.detail: Valve bans the players involved in the 2014 match-fixing case from its events.

entries.title: Animation and hitbox overhaul; M4A1-S changes
entries.detail: New player animations and hitboxes; the M4A1-S is changed.
entries.status: confirmed (patch); the size of the effect is our estimate

entries.title: Inferno returns; Dust II removed for rework
Dust II back in the competitive pool; Cobblestone out
CS:GO goes free to play
entries.detail: The player base grows; more talent appears in the lower tiers.

entries.title: Round-loss bonus reworked; AUG and M4A1-S tweaks
entries.detail: Loss bonuses now step down one level per win instead of resetting, which weakens the economic snowball. Comebacks become more likely.

entries.title: Cache leaves the competitive pool (Vertigo joins)
entries.detail: Vertigo is not in the game.

entries.title: COVID-19: LAN events move online
entries.detail: Tournaments are played online by region; the ESL One Rio Major is cancelled. LANs return gradually in late 2021.

entries.title: Coach spectator bug bans
entries.detail: Coaches who abused the spectator bug are banned (see the generated ban events).

entries.title: Anubis added; Dust II removed. AWP magazine cut to 5
entries.detail: The AWP magazine drops from 10 to 5 rounds, and the M4A1-S loses range.

entries.title: Counter-Strike 2 replaces CS:GO
entries.detail: Sub-tick servers and volumetric smokes change utility play: grenades and team coordination matter more.

entries.title: Valve Regional Standings decide invitations
entries.detail: Open circuit: invitations to the big events come from VRS (the mod's VRS feature switches on).
